title: Macros that save typing
description:
Write `macro_rules!` macros for common patterns.

```
hashmap!{"a" => 1, "b" => 2} = {"a": 1, "b": 2}
max!(3, 9, 4) = 9
check!(2 + 2 == 4) passed
check!(1 > 2) failed: 1 > 2
```
hints: `max!`: `($x:expr) => { $x };` and `($x:expr, $($rest:expr),+) => {{ let a = $x; let b = max!($($rest),+); if a > b { a } else { b } }};`.

`stringify!` is a built-in macro that turns tokens into a `&str` of their source text, without evaluating them: in a rule `($e:expr) => { ... }`, `stringify!($e)` for `check!(1 > 2)` gives `"1 > 2"`, while `$e` itself gives `false`.
requirements: `hashmap!` builds a `HashMap` from `key => value` pairs, with an optional trailing comma.
`max!` takes one or more expressions (recursion on the repetition).
`check!` prints the expression's own text with `stringify!`.
stretch: Write a `newtype!(Meters, f64)` macro that declares a struct and its `Display` impl.
